No patch hunks or head_text were included, so the actual change cannot be identified and nothing is cited on the head side. This is a coverage limit, not evidence that the change is safe. The file is documentation only. The base text describes build, CI cache and release-signing procedures, with no runtime security behaviour. Statements the next pass should check against any diff: (1) lines 243 and 314-317, 342-344 and 375-376: signing and publication run in separate jobs, signing verifies the same-run artifact's commit, version, inventory and entitlements before importing its certificate, and release caches never hold signing keys or notarized bundles (T-054, A-017, A-011). (2) Line 346-349: release-plumbing PRs run with PR-scoped caches and no signing or publishing secrets. (3) Lines 14-21: the Autopilot E2E harness uses an isolated test store and does not disable the production cohort gate (T-060, T-055). (4) Lines 131-135: the build does not enable payments or a live cohort. (5) Lines 251-263: the Bedrock review workflow uses a separate org-membership read token and hash-locked dependencies. (6) Lines 55-72: CI component routing skips expensive jobs for docs-only changes, while Release Integrity and Docs Lint stay unconditional. A diff that weakened any of these claims would be a threat-model gap. Pinned submodule SHAs at lines 453-456 are build provenance for the provider, which handles A-001 data (T-041 relevance is indirect).
